From: Alex Prior <alex.prior@novamed.com>

Cc: Nina Choi <nina.choi@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: sustained throughput loss during nightly ETL window

Evelyn —

Thanks for taking this. We saw a sustained degradation across 03:15–04:50 PT last night where our bulk inference pipelines fell from expected 2.5k TPS to ~400 TPS and a 15% 5xx rate. That window is when NovaMed ingests the previous day of patient reports; delays there cascade into our SLAs with hospitals.

Prelim data attached (throughput-analysis.csv). We need: 1) a clear root cause and timeline, 2) a commercial remediation proposal for the missed SLA, and 3) confirmation of steps to prevent recurrence.

This is now an executive-level issue for us; please escalate internally. We would like a readout with Redwood execs and our COO tomorrow if possible.

Alex
VP Ops — NovaMed Analytics

Attachments: throughput-analysis.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Alex —

First, I’m very sorry for the impact last night and thank you for the data. I’ve looped in Ben (Customer Success) and Marcus (Platform SRE) to lead the incident review and remediation. We’ll prioritize a timeline and an initial commercial position by EOD today.

Immediate next steps:
- Marcus will post an incident timeline and preliminary root cause within 3 hours.
- Ben will draft a remediation and credit framework tied to the actual minutes of unavailable capacity.
- I will coordinate an exec readout slot and bring a proposed settlement for your review.

We take this seriously and will also prepare a canary rollback plan to remove the change that correlated with the regression overnight (attachment: canary-rollback-plan.pdf).

Evelyn
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:27:00-07:00
Subject: Incident timeline — autoscaler regression + queuing 

Team —

Prelim notes from logs:
- 03:09 PT: rollout of autoscaler change that tightened the convolution of pod-provisioning policy.
- 03:15–03:42 PT: observed queue growth on ingress; CPU on serving instances pegged; tail latencies spiked and 503s rose to 14%.
- 03:42 PT: autoscaler entered a cooldown state and failed to provision additional hosts quickly due to a metric mislabel (metrics.v2 -> metrics.v3 mismatch).
- 03:42–04:50 PT: sustained degraded throughput. Recovery began after we force-rolled back the autoscaler policy at 04:51 PT.

Root cause: metric name mismatch in the autoscaler rule introduced in the April 24 release. This prevented scale decisions for a subset of GPU pools.

Mitigation actions completed: rollback applied 04:51 PT; temporary warm pool applied; KV cache primed for the longest-running pipelines. Longer term: add metric schema validation and an autoscaler canary gating.

I’ll prepare logs and a runbook excerpt for the customer readout.

Marcus
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: incident-logs-snippet.txt (included in Drive link)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Prior <alex.prior@novamed.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed remediation and commercial offer from Redwood

Alex / Nina —

Thanks for the patience while we dug through the telemetry. Below is our proposed remediation package, structured to be action-oriented and measurable. We’re open to adjustments but wanted to put a concrete offer on the table ahead of the exec readout.

Proposed package (short form):
1) One-time service credit: 50% of the invoiced monthly usage for the affected compute tier for April (applied as credit against May billing).
2) Temporary Dedicated Buffer: No-cost dedicated burst capacity for up to 72 hours per month for the next 2 months to cover peak windows while we implement autoscaler canaries.
3) Technical safeguards: priority code review for autoscaler rules, metric-schema validation, and a staged canary policy (we will deliver the canary plan in 48 hrs).
4) SLA amendment addendum: an elevated SLA for your critical ETL route for a 90-day window with a faster escalation path and weekly cadence.

We’ll also include a joint post-incident report and an implementation timeline. For transparency, the facts and timeline Marcus recorded will be part of that report.

Please review and let us know what parts you’d like tightened before the readout. If acceptable, I’ll surface this to our commercial execs for final sign-off prior to tomorrow’s meeting.

Ben Carter
Senior Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-remediation-terms.docx

From: Alex Prior <alex.prior@novamed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Choi <nina.choi@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed remediation and commercial offer from Redwood

Ben / Evelyn —

Appreciate the detailed package. NovaMed accepts the technical safeguards and the temporary dedicated buffer immediately; these help our ops team in the short term. On the commercial side we need either: a) a larger one-time credit (75% of April compute invoiced for the affected tier) OR b) a 50% credit plus a 6-month 25% discount on the next two dedicated tiers as a commitment to reliability while you complete the autoscaler canary rollout.

We’ll bring a final position to the readout once your execs confirm whether option (a) or (b) is possible. We also request a 30-minute run-through of the canary rollback plan with our SREs prior to the rollout.

Alex
VP Ops — NovaMed Analytics
